nodes.role: Resolves one immutable Mission identity plus repository and Mission anchor roots.
Creates one operation context for status, setup, tasks, next, workflow, and accept commands.
Keeps Git topology on the repository root while routing Mission artifacts through the Mission anchor.
Carries the Mission anchor through status reads, write-target resolution, and bookkeeping commits while retaining the repository root for Git policy.
Persists and rolls back coordination artifacts through a confined atomic write and unlink boundary.
Resolves task operations once and carries both repository and Mission anchor roots through task reads, status transitions, and coordination commits.
Reads status and acceptance evidence from the selected Mission anchor without changing managed-worktree behavior.
Covers conflict safety, two linked worktrees, lifecycle commands, indexing cost, and primary-checkout immutability.
Scans every production source and prevents lifecycle consumers from introducing a second Mission-root authority outside a shrink-only reviewed allowlist.
Covers Windows confined writes and unlinks plus transaction rollback and owner projection semantics.

flow: CLI command receives a Mission selector in any same-repository linked worktree.
MissionOperationContext resolves repository_root, mission_anchor_root, and immutable identity once.
Lifecycle and task readers and writers retain repository_root for Git topology and use mission_anchor_root for Mission artifacts.
The coordination transaction persists generated artifacts through the confined atomic writer and restores them through the same boundary.
Conflicting identities fail before writes; managed worktrees retain their existing placement behavior.
